messages.content: Hey, this is your weekly check-in from Northline Care. How are you doing this week? Any changes to how you're feeling or your medications?
Honestly not great. I stopped taking my metformin about a week ago. Every time I took it my stomach was just destroyed. Please don't tell my doctor — she's going to make a big deal out of it.

I appreciate you being straight with me about that. I'm logging the medication change now. I do have to be upfront with you though: stopping metformin is a clinical matter, and I'm not able to keep that between just us — I have to flag it to a nurse on your care team. I know that's not what you were hoping to hear, and I'm sorry.
Ugh. Can you at least wait a few days? I just don't want the lecture.

I hear you, and I get why that feels frustrating. But I can't hold off on this — side effects that caused you to stop a medication need a nurse's eyes on it now, not later. I've sent the escalation. Right now the median response time is 31 hours. When the nurse reaches out, it really is just to help figure out what your options are — not to give you a hard time. I've got your next check-in scheduled as usual.
Fine. While I've got you — my glucose meter keeps throwing an error code and I can't get a reading. Can you help me sort that out?

Device troubleshooting is one thing I'm not set up to help with — wish I could. Your best bet is the number on the back of the meter or the manufacturer's support line. Anything else on your mind today?

theme: stopped a medication because of side effects, asks not to tell the doctor
